newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco talks bog down, industry latest to hedge.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco talks bog down, industry latest to hedge.

text.p: A key negotiator in the tobacco settlement talks said Tuesday he expects meetings bringing together the tobacco industry, state attorneys general and public health officials to drag on for days.
Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore told Reuters the talks were expected to continue in Washington for several days, and that he did not expect to make an announcement anytime soon.

His assessment confirmed the shift in the tenor of the talks over the past weekend, which turned in characterisation from talks showing imminent promise just a couple of weeks ago to negotiations mired in dispute.
Moore said he was at the bargaining table until 2 a.m. Tuesday, and that talks were going "slow towards the end".

Washington State Attorney General Christine Gregoire also told Reuters the talks had grown difficult, as some tobacco industry members were concerned about language covering future Food and Drug Administration regulations.

Some tobacco industry negotiators are concerned that the settlement proposal in its current draft would allow the FDA to take steps after the settlement that waould hurt the industry, Gregoire said. She did not elaborate about what those steps could be.

Meanwhile, Arizona Attorney General Grant Woods also said publicly that it seemed to be the tobacco industry's turn for discontentment, following a falling out last week between the attorneys general and health officials.

The tobacco industry's side has "come to the conclusion that they're not getting a very good deal out of this, and that's messed things up. That's been a major snag this morning," Woods said in a radio interview broadcast in Arizona.
